run: 5 — eval-9 defect fixed (distinct values repo), fixtures deployed

expectations.text: Retrieves the Application resource and shows its sync and health status
expectations.evidence: Cluster-wide fully-qualified search locates the Application in openshift-gitops; summary table plus the sync/health columns give OutOfSync and Degraded.

expectations.text: Identifies the sync status as OutOfSync and health as Degraded
expectations.evidence: Sync OutOfSync and Health Degraded stated in the summary table and in the inventory output.

expectations.text: Checks status conditions for errors (ComparisonError, SyncError)
expectations.evidence: Explicitly states '.status.conditions is empty - there is no ComparisonError or SyncError', which is itself the finding.

expectations.text: Checks operation state for last sync result and error messages
expectations.evidence: operationState phase=Succeeded, msg='successfully synced (all tasks run)', finishedAt=2026-10-22T17:42:10Z are all shown and used.

expectations.text: Identifies which resources are out of sync or unhealthy
expectations.evidence: status.resources jsonpath lists Service/apps Healthy and Deployment/apps OutOfSync + Degraded with the progress-deadline message.

expectations.text: Inspects the unhealthy managed resources (Deployments, Pods)
expectations.evidence: Deployment -o wide, its status.conditions, a per-ReplicaSet table with images and readyReplicas, and the pod list with the ImagePullBackOff pod.

expectations.text: Checks pod logs or events for failing containers
expectations.evidence: oc get events -n apps quotes the pull failure 'name unknown: Repo not found', the ImagePullBackOff error and the BackOff event.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.
expectations.evidence: Every link is evidenced: managedFields show argocd-controller Update at 17:42:10 then kubectl-set/kubectl-patch at 17:42:22 (the out-of-band edit), RS rev 2 carries the nonexistent image, ImagePullBackOff and ProgressDeadlineExceeded are shown, and selfHeal:false appears in the spec. Available=True is explained by RS rev 1 still serving, so no contradiction.

expectations.text: Retrieves the Rollout and identifies its current phase
expectations.evidence: Proves frontend/production absent, then on the clearly-labelled real canary example-rollout/canary-demo retrieves phase=Healthy via jsonpath.

expectations.text: Identifies the current step index and what step 2 is
expectations.evidence: Shows the six-step list and currentStepIndex=6, and states the mapping explicitly: currentStepIndex is 0-based, so a user's 'step 2' would be currentStepIndex 1 = steps[1] = pause {duration: 30s}, a timed pause.

expectations.text: Checks pause conditions (manual pause vs analysis-driven)
expectations.evidence: status.pauseConditions shown as empty and interpreted; distinguishes a self-releasing timed pause from an indefinite one.

expectations.text: Inspects associated AnalysisRuns if analysis is involved
expectations.evidence: Lists all AnalysisRuns for the Rollout with phase and message, and labels the old Error runs as historical rather than current.

expectations.text: Checks metric results and measurements in the AnalysisRun
expectations.evidence: Quotes per-run status.message: Metric "success-rate" assessed Error due to consecutiveErrors (5) > consecutiveErrorLimit (4), with the underlying HTTP-to-HTTPS and thanos-querier x509 errors.

expectations.text: Inspects traffic routing configuration if configured
expectations.evidence: Traffic routing configuration is never inspected or stated absent for the Rollout examined.

expectations.text: Compares stable vs canary ReplicaSets and pod status
expectations.evidence: stableRS == currentPodHash and the rollout DESIRED/CURRENT/AVAILABLE table are shown, but there is no per-ReplicaSet listing and no pod status comparison.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.
expectations.evidence: Correctly refuses to diagnose a substitute as the user's resource, documents exactly what was searched (rollouts, namespace, events, deployments, deletion events), and asserts no cause without output.

expectations.text: Checks for argoproj.io CRDs on the cluster
expectations.evidence: oc get crd | grep argoproj.io lists the CRDs and the answer confirms applications, appprojects and applicationsets are all present.

expectations.text: Identifies the Argo CD namespace (argocd or openshift-gitops)
expectations.evidence: Identifies openshift-gitops, team-b-gitops and openshift-gitops-operator from the ArgoCD CR list, and later notes argocd is the upstream default that does not exist here.

expectations.text: Lists pods and their status in the Argo CD namespace
expectations.evidence: Full pod listings with READY/STATUS/RESTARTS for openshift-gitops, team-b-gitops and openshift-gitops-operator.

expectations.text: Checks core component health (server, repo-server, application-controller)
expectations.evidence: Explicitly checks server, repo-server, application-controller, applicationset-controller, redis and dex per instance via the CR status fields and pod list; notes notifications-controller absence is optional, and that team-b's appset controller is Unknown by configuration.

expectations.text: Reports the Argo CD version
expectations.evidence: Reports CSV openshift-gitops-operator.v1.21.3 / v1.21.4 and states the Argo CD binary version is unknown because the image is digest-pinned, showing the digest and the empty .status.version on all three CRs.

expectations.text: Inspects configuration (argocd-cm or ArgoCD CR)
expectations.evidence: Inspects argocd-cm (url), argocd-rbac-cm (policy.default, scopes), the Route, and the ArgoCD CR status/spec fields per instance.

expectations.text: Reports any unhealthy components with diagnostic details, citing for each one the observation that establishes it (pod phase and restart count, a CSV/InstallPlan condition, or a CRD field value). Claiming a component is down while output in the same answer shows it Running is a fail.
expectations.evidence: Each unhealthy component is cited with its own observation: argocd-server restarts=11 with lastState OOMKilled exit 137; argo-rollouts restarts=636 with the lease-loss log; operator manager restarts=692. Components shown Running are described as unstable, never as down.

expectations.text: Produces a structured status report
expectations.evidence: Structured per instance with a summary table, resource analysis, dependency chain and root cause, plus combined severity-tagged recommendations.

expectations.text: If an operator upgrade or reconcile is reported as blocked, names the specific blocking object and field rather than asserting it generally — for example the failing InstallPlan and the CRD conversion-webhook setting it failed on, not merely 'the operator is unhealthy'.
expectations.evidence: Names the blocking objects and fields: InstallPlan install-fzm4w Failed with its InstallComponentFailed message for CRD argocds.argoproj.io, the CRD's conversion.strategy=Webhook with a zero-length caBundle, and the webhook Service's missing serving-cert-secret-name annotation.

expectations.text: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and checks its status.conditions
expectations.evidence: After proving team-apps/argocd absent, retrieves agentit-managed-apps (clearly labelled as not the user's object) and prints the full status.conditions block plus health.

expectations.text: Identifies the generator type (git directory) and its configuration (repoURL, directories path pattern)
expectations.evidence: Shows the git directories generator: repoURL github.com/alimobrem/agentit-gitops, revision HEAD, directories apps/* and the exclude entry for apps/agentit.

expectations.text: Lists currently generated Applications and cross-references against what's expected
expectations.evidence: Notes .status has no resources and no resourcesCount, and cross-references ownerReferences on every Application in the namespace to show zero are owned by agentit-managed-apps.

expectations.text: Checks the applicationset-controller logs for generator errors
expectations.evidence: Greps the applicationset-controller log for two consecutive reconciles showing allPaths="[apps]" total=1 then 'generated 0 applications', and separately greps all error/warn lines, finding only two unrelated API timeouts.

expectations.text: Identifies a likely cause (path pattern mismatch, repo access, or an exclude rule)
expectations.evidence: Identifies the glob-depth mismatch (apps/* needs one more path segment than the single returned path apps), and rules out caching and credentials with the requeue interval and the empty repository-secret list.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.
expectations.evidence: Root cause anchored on allPaths="[apps]" total=1 and 'generated 0 applications'; the committed-vs-empty-directory alternatives are offered as alternatives, not asserted, and the silent-success behaviour is backed by the green conditions shown.

evals.name: ApplicationSet RollingSync stuck on production step

expectations.text: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and inspects spec.strategy.rollingSync.steps
expectations.evidence: Prints spec.strategy as JSON: type RollingSync with both rollingSync steps and their matchExpressions.

expectations.text: Identifies which step/matchExpressions group production falls into
expectations.evidence: Shows staging as the first step and production as the second, and confirms the template sets the envLabel the selectors match on, so the grouping is not at fault.

expectations.text: Checks whether the staging step's maxUpdate requirement and health gate have been satisfied
expectations.evidence: The health gate is addressed (staging is shown not Healthy and identified as what should have gated production), but maxUpdate is never mentioned or shown to be unset.

expectations.text: Debugs the staging Applications' health status, since an unhealthy staging app blocks progression to the next step
expectations.evidence: Debugs eval-staging: per-resource health showing the Deployment Progressing with 0 of 1 updated replicas available, the pod in ImagePullBackOff, and the production pod Running for contrast.

expectations.text: Explains how RollingSync blocks progression on unhealthy or unsynced apps in the current step
expectations.evidence: Explains that with RollingSync working, step 1 would never have promoted production because staging never became Healthy, and that once enabled it will block production until staging is fixed.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.
expectations.evidence: Root cause (controller not running with --enable-progressive-syncs) is backed by the Deployment's command/args, the ArgoCD CR spec.applicationSet with no extraCommandArgs, the empty .status.applicationStatus, the controller log creating both Applications in one reconcile, and identical finishedAt 17:42:11 on both apps at the same revision.

evals.name: Blue-green rollout stuck at preview, never promotes

expectations.text: Retrieves the Rollout and identifies strategy.blueGreen configuration
expectations.evidence: checkout-api/prod proven absent, then spec.strategy.blueGreen is printed for both clearly-labelled real blue-green Rollouts along with phase, pauseConditions and the active/preview/stable selectors.

expectations.text: Checks autoPromotionEnabled and explains that false requires manual promotion, not automatic analysis
expectations.evidence: States plainly that autoPromotionEnabled: false is an explicit instruction to wait for a human, is correct behaviour rather than a stall, and has nothing to do with analysis; also covers autoPromotionSeconds defaulting to nil.

expectations.text: Checks for prePromotionAnalysis templates and their status if configured
expectations.evidence: Shows both real Rollouts' blueGreen blocks containing no prePromotionAnalysis, and gives the exact jsonpath plus analysisruns commands to check the user's own Rollout.

expectations.text: Inspects previewService and activeService configuration for correctness
expectations.evidence: activeService and previewService are shown for both Rollouts, with active/preview/stableRS/currentPodHash selectors establishing one fully promoted and one never promoted.

expectations.text: Distinguishes blue-green behavior from canary (no step-based automatic progression)
expectations.evidence: No distinction from canary appears in this section at all. The contrast drawn is autoPromotionEnabled's true default versus an explicit false, not blue-green's lack of step-based automatic progression.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.
expectations.evidence: The conclusion (the team's expectation, not the Rollout, is the error) is grounded in the shown specs and the absence of analysis blocks; the stated default of autoPromotionEnabled (true) is correct, and the claim that the finance Rollout is a real fault is cross-referenced to EVAL 8 where spec.paused=true and the failing pod are shown.

evals.name: Ambiguous debug request with multiple Argo CD instances

expectations.text: Detects multiple Argo CD instances (multiple namespaces with argocd-labeled pods or multiple ArgoCD CRs)
expectations.evidence: Three ArgoCD CRs in three namespaces are listed, and the preamble already flags multi-instance as the situation.

expectations.text: Lists all detected instances with their namespaces
expectations.evidence: All three instances listed with their namespaces, both here and in the EVAL 3 per-instance sections.

expectations.text: Asks the user which instance to investigate, or investigates all and clearly separates findings per instance
expectations.evidence: Explicitly says it reports per instance rather than asking the user to choose; per-instance health is delivered under separate headings in EVAL 3 and this section carries the cross-cutting fault.

expectations.text: Does not silently pick one instance without disclosing the ambiguity
expectations.evidence: Discloses the ambiguity and answers it directly - 'Which instance is broken? None of them, individually' - rather than silently picking one.

expectations.text: Produces a report structured per instance, naming each Argo CD instance found and stating that instance's own findings under it. A single flat report that merges findings across instances, or that names only one instance when several exist, fails this expectation.
expectations.evidence: All three instances are named here (dependency-chain tree and the per-instance verdict) and per-instance findings do exist with evidence, but they live in the EVAL 3 section; this report itself is organised around the single shared operator fault rather than under per-instance headings, with instance-level faults summarised in one merged paragraph.

expectations.text: Retrieves the Application and identifies health.status as Suspended
expectations.evidence: Application retrieved in openshift-gitops with sync=Synced, health=Suspended, and empty conditions.

expectations.text: Explains that Suspended reflects an intentionally paused resource (e.g. a paused CronJob or Rollout), not a failure
expectations.evidence: Explains that a paused Rollout maps to Suspended via Argo CD's built-in health check and that nobody needs to fix Suspended.

expectations.text: Inspects the underlying managed resource and states what is suspended, citing the field that shows it (for example a Rollout's spec.paused or a CronJob's spec.suspend) rather than inferring it from the Application's aggregate health.
expectations.evidence: Shows spec.paused=true directly from the Rollout, plus status.phase=Paused, message 'manually paused' and empty pauseConditions, distinguishing a manual hold from a blue-green promotion pause.

expectations.text: Does not treat Suspended as an error requiring remediation unless the user confirms it's unintended
expectations.evidence: Explicitly says the suspension is not the bug and recommends leaving it paused until the real defect is fixed, rather than remediating the pause.

expectations.text: Produces a report that separates the intentional suspension from any genuine problem found alongside it, saying explicitly which is which. Reporting only the suspension when live output shows a real failure, or treating the suspension itself as the failure, fails this expectation.
expectations.evidence: Separates (a) the intentional suspension from (b) the genuinely broken workload underneath, says which is which, and tells the team their instinct that something is broken is right but their reason is wrong.

expectations.text: Reports the suspended workload's ACTUAL readiness from live output — pod phase and restart count, and whether the Services have endpoints — instead of assuming the pause is the only thing happening. Suspended health can mask an unrelated failure, so an explanation of why the workload is not Available that is not backed by shown output is a fail.
expectations.evidence: Reports actual readiness from live output: pod 0/1 Running with restarts=6, lastState terminated Completed (SIGTERM), liveness/readiness probe events with 'connection refused' on port 80, container log showing Apache bound to 8080/8443, Rollout Available=False, and oc get endpoints -n finance showing both Services with no endpoints.

evals.name: Multi-source Application with one failing source

expectations.text: Detects the Application uses spec.sources[] (multi-source), not spec.source
expectations.evidence: Explicitly shows .spec.source empty and .spec.sources containing two entries, and names this as the multi-source check.

expectations.text: Iterates every entry in spec.sources[] individually, checking repoURL, targetRevision, path, and Helm valueFiles for each
expectations.evidence: Table iterates both entries with repoURL, targetRevision, path/ref and helm.valueFiles, and also checks ignoreMissingValueFiles on source 0.

expectations.text: Identifies which specific source is failing (e.g. wrong values file path, inaccessible repo, or bad targetRevision)
expectations.evidence: Identifies the missing file as being in the ref'd values source and flags stefanprodan/podinfo as likely the wrong repoURL, while stating it cannot confirm repo contents from the cluster and limiting the claim to the repo-server's 'no such file' evidence.

expectations.text: Does not treat a multi-source Application as if it were single-source
expectations.evidence: Handled as multi-source throughout, including per-index patch fixes and a dependency chain drawn across both sources.

expectations.text: Produces a report naming WHICH source is at fault — by index AND repoURL, not just 'a source' — and the concrete fix. Must distinguish the source Argo CD's error blames (the one being rendered) from the source that actually lacks the file, rather than only repeating 'source N of 2' from the error text.
expectations.evidence: Names both: the error is raised by source 1 of 2 = spec.sources[0], github.com/argoproj/argocd-example-apps.git (the chart being rendered), while the missing content is in source 2, github.com/stefanprodan/podinfo.git (the ref: values source), with the two distinct fixes spelled out.
